finding.text: The main proof (deliverable 3) is missing. There is no proof.txt in the task dir or in the worktree (qf-2), yet Servex/doc/dormant.md:683 links to it. Only compact-proof.txt exists. Still unproven: 4 agents with 3 dormant leaving one claude.exe in `tasklist`, a dormant agent answering within 15 s with its context intact, and 8 minions showing 5 working and 3 queued, then draining.

Dormant agents now pile up forever and eventually block every spawn. The sweep used to `stop()` finished minions (Global.js:424, removed). Now they only sleep, and Lifecycle.js:207/252 reaps `idle` agents only, so nothing ever removes a dormant one from `live`. But `admit()` still counts every non-stopped agent against the 30 ceiling (Global.js:462-464). After about 30 finished minions, any spawn without a live parent is refused, and the queue waits forever. Either leave `dormant` out of that count, or stop a finished minion whose parent has landed.

A task mastermind with one finished minion is never status-checked again. Heartbeat.children() (Heartbeat.js:197) counts any child that is not `stopped`, and a dormant minion is not stopped. So `if (this.children(t.owner).length) continue` (Heartbeat.js:126) skips a stuck parent for good. Count only `working`/`starting`/`idle` children, or a queued one.

The cap only gates new spawns. `send()` wakes a dormant agent straight into `working` (Agents.js `awaken`), and `admit()` lets any resume through (Global.js:457). So heartbeat checks, card replies and child reports can still push the working count past 5. That is a sound choice (a wake must deliver its message, and the child ending its turn usually frees a slot), but "at most 5 working" is not guaranteed. Say so in dormant.md.

A dormant task mastermind with no children is still sent a heartbeat status check after 5 silent minutes (Heartbeat.js:133). That starts a new process, which sleeps again 3 minutes later. The answered-count backoff limits the churn, but a check could skip dormant owners whose task log is simply waiting.
"working N/5" appears in heartbeat_status and in the Monitor verdict (Monitor.js:80). The requirement also names the dashboard, and nothing in the diff shows that the dashboard page renders it.
Deliverable 4 and the live-machine memory numbers (before and after the merge) are not done yet. That is expected before the merge, but the landing must include them.

Compaction works: 103k → 10.5k tokens, and the secret word survived (compact-proof.txt). But the memory restart only took the process from 256 MB to 229 MB, so the 500 MB checkpoint-and-restart path saves little. Measure it on a genuinely large agent before relying on it.

Simpler: Global.reaper() wraps `agents.register` to trigger the queue drain (Global.js:401-402). Calling `kick()` from Agent.result() or settle() through the host would avoid wrapping another object's method.
